question: Does a richer post-hoc calibrator fit on the registered CAL split improve EVAL top-label ECE of the frozen scale-002 fit100 model without degrading NLL/Brier? (classifier, features and margins frozen)

source.review_verdict: PASS (independent reviewer, distinct from author; 0 critical/high, 2 medium, 9 low)
source.baseline_model: scale-002 fit100 (job 20261011-ws-step2-scale-f2-recovery-author-001), parent LightGBM 10-class iteration 195 + 2 binary heads, seed 20261043

metric_definitions.classwise_ece_secondary: mean over 7 leaves of per-leaf 10-bin ECE
metric_definitions.bootstrap: whole-game paired, 10000 draws, seed 20261211, unit game_pk, pitch-weighted ratio of game sums, ECE from per-game bin sums, percentile 95% CI

C2.name: Dirichlet ODIR (parent, lambda selected 0.01 by 5-fold game-grouped CV in CAL) + Platt heads (= C1 heads)

C3.name: per-leaf isotonic (PAV) on C0 seven-leaf probabilities, clip 1e-6, renormalised

paired_EVAL_differences_arm_minus_C0.note: differences rounded to 7 decimals here; exact values in the job result.json

interpretation: No pre-registered alternative improves EVAL top-label ECE with a CI excluding zero. C1 (vector scaling) has the best point ECE (0.00243 vs 0.00356) and is non-inferior on NLL/Brier, but its ECE CI covers zero (-0.0026, +0.0018). C3 (isotonic) fits CAL best in-sample yet degrades EVAL NLL by +0.00114 (CI above zero), exceeding the +0.0010 margin: overfitting of the CAL split. The baseline ECE is already ~0.0036 (0.36 percentage points of top-label confidence), so the calibration headroom is small relative to the game-level sampling noise of 275 games. Fan-facing value of a calibrator swap: none demonstrable; the confidence numbers shown would move by well under one percentage point. Follow-up only if ECE is measured on a larger EVAL window or on service-relevant subgroups; a classifier change (not a calibrator) is the lever for NLL/Brier.
